title: Platform systems & services — playbook, runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap (Q2 2026 addendum)
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Changelog (short):
- 2026-02-15 by Asha Kapoor: Q2 2026 addendum with updated telemetry/resilience roadmap and runbook links.

Overview:

This document is the canonical playbook for Platform Engineering systems and services: it consolidates the current inventory, SLOs, dashboards and alerting standards, operational runbooks for high-severity incidents and common mitigations, a short how‑to section for routine platform tasks, a Q2 2026 roadmap, and a brief retrospective on major reliability work completed in the last two quarters. The audience is platform engineers, SREs, and on-call responders.

Scope and ownership:

- Scope: control plane services, service mesh and ingress, telemetry pipeline (Prometheus/Grafana/Tempo/Jaeger), alerting, platform CI/CD runners, cluster autoscaling controller, and storage provisioning.
- Excluded: model serving runtime internals (see eng-serving-runtime), customer-facing API product feature specs (see product-docs).
- Primary owners: Platform Systems team (oncall: platform-systems@redwood.com).

Systems inventory (summary):

1) control-plane-api
   - Owner: Platform Systems
   - Purpose: central config API for dedicated and private deployment control plane
   - Primary SLO: 99.95% availability (monthly), P50 latency < 50 ms for control operations

2) telemetry-pipeline
   - Owner: Observability Guild / Platform Systems
   - Purpose: ingest + long-term retention of metrics/traces/logs (Prometheus remote write -> Cortex; Tempo for traces; Loki for logs)
   - Primary SLO: 99.9% successful ingest within 60s; alerting lag < 5m

3) cluster-autoscaler-v2
   - Owner: Platform Systems
   - Purpose: scale node pools and node groups for Dedicated workloads
   - Primary SLO: scaling-decision latency < 60s for burst events; capacity provisioning success rate > 99%

4) ci-runners
   - Owner: Developer Experience (eng-developer-experience) with Platform Systems support
   - Purpose: hosted Kubernetes runners for pipelines and integration tests
   - Primary SLO: queue wait < 5m for standard tier; job success rate > 98%

SLOs and alerting standards (how we set thresholds):

- SLO tiers: Critical (99.95%), High (99.9%), Standard (99.5%). Service owner selects tier; Platform Systems will review for capacity implications.
- Error budget burn alerts: Email/SMS at 50% burn in 7 days, Slack @oncall at 80% burn in 72 hours, Pager at 100% burn or if burn rate predicts 100% within 24 hours.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 reported on dashboards; p95/p99 exceeding baseline by 2x for 10m triggers an incident candidate alert.
- On-call paging policy: Only page for P1/P0 (see oncall section). P2/P3 create tickets in Jira and notify owners in Slack.

Standard alerts (examples):

- control-plane-api_5xx_rate_high
  - Condition: 5xx rate > 1% of requests for 5m and absolute 5xx > 10/min
  - Severity: P1
  - Runbook: control-plane-api-runbook (link below)

- telemetry-ingest-lag
  - Condition: Prometheus remote-write ingestion lag > 60s (5m window) OR missing telemetry from > 2 critical services
  - Severity: P1 (affects all downstream alerting/SLIs)
  - Runbook: telemetry-pipeline-runbook

- cluster-autoscaler-provision-failure
  - Condition: node provisioning failure rate > 5% for 10m OR > 2 failure events in 15m
  - Severity: P1/P2 depending on number of affected clusters

Dashboards (must-haves and ownership):

- Platform Overview (owner: Platform Systems): top-line availability, error budget burn, cluster capacity heatmap, global request rates.
- Telemetry Health (owner: Observability Guild): ingest lag, retention queue sizes, Cortex ingesters by replica, Tempo ingestion, Loki ingestion and tail latency.
- Control Plane (owner: Platform Systems): control-plane API latency histograms, 5xx/4xx breakdown, active config rollouts.
- CI Runners (owner: Developer Experience): queue depth, runner utilization by instance type, recent test flakiness rate.
- Cost & Capacity (owner: Platform Costing): GPU/CPU pool utilization, pending spot eviction rates, reservation usage percentage.

Each dashboard must include: owner, primary viewers, and a short 'what to watch' blurb that appears at the top of the dashboard. Dashboards are stored in Grafana and managed via the grafana-provisioning repo (PRs required for changes).

Runbooks (operational playbooks):

Canonical runbooks and where to find them:
- control-plane-api-runbook (Grafana playlist: /dashboards/control-plane; repo: infra/control-plane/runbooks)
- telemetry-pipeline-runbook (repo: infra/observability/runbooks)
- cluster-autoscaler-runbook (repo: infra/cluster-autoscaler/runbooks)
- ci-runners-degraded-performance (repo: infra/ci-runners/runbooks)

Example runbook excerpt: control-plane-api P1 outage

1) Triage (first 10 minutes):
   - Confirm scope: which zones/regions and customer tiers affected (hosted/dedicated/private).
   - Check Platform Overview dashboard and control-plane API traces (Tempo).
   - Identify top 5 error signatures (e.g., DB timeouts, auth failures, downstream rate limit).

2) Immediate mitigations:
   - If DB contention suspected: scale read-replicas, enable query offload routing, or roll back recent schema/infra changes.
   - If auth/service mesh problem: toggle fallback auth provider (feature flag) or roll back the last Istio/Envoy change.

3) Communication:
   - Post to #incidents with summary: "P1 control-plane-api — affected: X services, start: HH:MM UTC, mitigation: Y".
   - Update status page and incident bridge (call: +1-555-0100).

4) Recovery and postmortem actions:
   - If mitigation > 30m, collect heap/CPU profiles, core dumps, and create a dedicated Jira ticket for RCA.
   - Implement follow-up remediation within 3 business days for hotfix; longer-term work to be scheduled in roadmap.

How-to (routine platform tasks):

- Adding a dashboard:
  1) Fork grafana/provisioning/dashboards/<team> and add dashboard JSON.
  2) Add metadata top-lines: owner, description, primary viewers, alert bindings.
  3) Open a PR and request review from Observability Guild and Platform Systems. Expect 48h review SLA for emergency changes.

- Creating or tuning an alert:
  1) Scope the SLI and create a query in the Telemetry Health dashboard.
  2) Use the alerting playbook template: name, condition, severity, owner, runbook link, 1-3 mitigations.
  3) Run an alert dry-run for 24–72 hours (metric recording with no page) to validate signal; then enable paging.

- Runbook updates and ownership changes:
  - Keep runbook in the infra repo README with oncall rotation and contact details. Any ownership change requires a PR + reviewer from Platform Systems and a Slack mention to #platform-ops.

Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities):

1) Telemetry resilience project (owner: Observability Guild)
   - Goals: reduce Tempo ingestion latency to < 3s for 95% of traces, reduce Prometheus remote-write loss to < 0.05% per week.
   - Milestones: streaming rewrite (May 2026), autoscaling for ingesters (June 2026), retention-cost model (end of Q2).

2) Autoscaler v2 stability & preemption safety (owner: Platform Systems)
   - Goals: deterministic node provisioning for Dedicated tiers, reduce provisioning failure events by 90%.
   - Milestones: canary rollout to low-risk clusters (April), multi-region rollback test (May), full rollout (June).

3) Operational observability (owner: Platform Systems + Developer Experience)
   - Goals: standardize per-service 'what to watch' and alert templates, onboard top 30 platform services to new templates.
   - Milestones: templates published (April), onboarding drive (May–June).

Retrospective (major work and learnings since Q4 2025):

- Telemetry refactor (Q4 2025–Q1 2026) resulted in 3x lower tail latency but surfaced an operational gap: missing runbooks for partial ingestion outages. Action: created telemetry-pipeline-runbook and a dashboard focused on partial loss modes.
- CI runner capacity shortages during major release (Dec 2025): root cause was low priority scheduling policy and stale autoscaler settings. Action: changed FIFO policy for release-critical jobs and added runner autoscaler tuning; observed queue wait drop from median 12m to 2m.
- Incident paging noise (Nov 2025): our alert thresholds were too sensitive on p95 for non-critical paths. Action: instituted alert dry-run window and rebalanced p95/p99 triggers; pages reduced by ~40% and attention to true P1s improved.

On-call, incident process, and SLAs:

- On-call rotations: 2-week rotation for Platform Systems primary oncall, with a backup oncall for weekends. Schedule maintained in the team calendar (platform-oncall-calendar).
- Pager escalation: P1 -> Primary oncall (pager) -> secondary after 10m -> Eng Director if unresolved after 60m.
- Incident postmortem: required for any incident > 30m with customer impact or if error budget burned > 10%. Postmortem template: timeline, contributing factors, corrective actions, owners, ETA.

Operational housekeeping and runbook maintenance cadence:

- Quarterly review of all runbooks and dashboards: owners get an automated reminder 30 days before review due.
- Any change that affects paging must pass a 72-hour dry-run before being enabled for production paging.

Appendix: useful links and CLI snippets:

- Grafana dashboards repo: https://git.redwood.com/grafana/provisioning/dashboards
- Runbooks repo: https://git.redwood.com/infra/runbooks
- Oncall Slack channels: #platform-ops, #observability, #incidents
- CLI: To quickly grab recent 5xx traces for control-plane-api:
  - kubectl -n platform logs deployment/control-plane-api --since=10m | grep "ERROR" | head -n 200
  - tempo-query --service control-plane-api --from=10m --limit=100

- Contact points:
  - Platform Systems Pager: +1-555-0100 (external incident bridge), platform-oncall@redwood.com
  - Observability Guild: observability@redwood.com

If you are updating this document: include a short changelog entry at the top of the body with date and author, and add yourself to the reviewers list if you made operational changes.
